requiredBeforeReady: Pass the clean canonical Docker x86-64 build, cumulative artifact probe, restart, and player-readiness validation.
scope: Restore the Publish 14.1 Combat Medic healMind command as an authenticated real-client transaction against a creature pet, including Mind treatment, healer wounds and battle fatigue, exact cleanup, and reproducible evidence.

findings: The retained pre-CU command table registers healMind to the actor hook healMind with optional other targeting, five-second default time, nonqueued dispatch, and client visibility two.
science_combatmedic_healing_range_speed_04 grants healMind; the novice box contributes combat_medic_effectiveness=5 and establishes the minimum treatment power used by the fixture.

Pinned Core3 requires a living Combat Medic and another healable player or creature pet within five meters and line of sight, at least 250 current Mind as a threshold, and actual Mind damage on the target.

Treatment power is (random 0..500 + 800) multiplied by combat_medic_effectiveness and the healer battle-fatigue ratio. Five percent of the amount healed becomes wounds in the healer's Mind, Focus, and Willpower plus equal battle fatigue; the 250 Mind value is not directly charged.

The retained healing library's older heal-mind constants diverge from the executable Core3 command behavior; the pinned command implementation governs restored semantics while the library supplies compatible pool, wound, battle-fatigue, effect, and PvP primitives.

eligibility: another living player or creature pet that is neither a droid nor an ordinary AI creature
PvP-helpable target within five meters and line of sight
healer current Mind at least 250 and target with positive Mind damage

campHealingObserver.payload: target receives healer object id plus native authoritative applied Mind delta

liveFixture.cleanupPolicy: destroy the fixture pet, source, and durable PCD; restore Mind maximum/current, Mind/Focus/Willpower wounds, battle fatigue, skill points, fixture-granted skills, and prior pet-master attachment; then prove repeated cleanup idempotence
